Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Isaac Newton born?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.

Named after two French physicists who discovered it in 1820, this equation in magnetostatics relates a magnetic field to the strength, direction, and distance of an electric current — which physics rule?
Biot–Savart law: Law of classical electromagnetism.
This rigid organ not only supports the body and enables movement but also manufactures both red and white blood cells and stores essential minerals — what is it?
Bone: Rigid organs of the skeleton of vertebrates.

Marketed as Wellbutrin, this atypical antidepressant doubles as a stop-smoking aid and stands out for not causing sexual dysfunction or weight gain — what is this norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor?
Bupropion: Medication mainly used for depression and smoking cessation.
This golden fungus — also known as 'girolle' — is often confused with a poisonous lookalike, though it remains a prized edible mushroom and the type species of its genus — which one is it?
Cantharellus cibarius: Species of fungus. Despite its characteristic features, C. cibarius can be confused with species such as the poisonous Omphalotus illudens.
Marketed as Zinacef and used against everything from meningitis to Lyme disease, this second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic was patented in 1971 — which drug?
Cefuroxime: Antibiotic medication. It is used by mouth or by injection into a vein or muscle.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
This little Indo-Pacific reef fish, banded in white, shelters among stinging tentacles and repays the favor by fending off anemone-eaters and fanning its host clean. What fish is it?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
This practice of secure communication sits at the intersection of math, computer science, and electrical engineering, and underpins e-commerce and chip-based payment cards — what is it called?
Cryptography: Practice and study of secure communication techniques.

Also nicknamed 'the bends,' this diving-related condition happens when dissolved gases form bubbles in body tissue during a too-rapid ascent, often settling painfully in the knees and elbows — what is it called?
Decompression sickness: Disorder caused by dissolved gases forming bubbles in tissues.

Sudden lower-abdominal pain, sometimes a 'smoldering' slow burn over days — and the trouble is little abnormal pouches inflaming in the wall of your large intestine. What gastrointestinal disease is this?
Diverticulitis: Digestive disease of the large intestine. People may experience a single attack, repeated attacks, or ongoing "smoldering" diverticulitis.
Also known as dropsy, this medical condition involves fluid buildup in body tissue, often causing swelling in the legs or arms — what is it?
Edema: Accumulation of excess fluid in tissue.
Caused by mutations in any of sixteen genes that weaken the skin's structural attachment layers, this rare inherited condition causes painful blistering from the slightest friction — which disease?
Epidermolysis bullosa: Rare medical conditions that result in easy blistering of the skin and mucous membranes.
This small woodland bird has blue-gray upperparts, a black eye-stripe, and famously plasters the entrance to its tree-hole nest with mud if it's too large — what is it?
Eurasian nuthatch: Small passerine bird species.
Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed to produce hybrids, this slender mustelid averages about 50 centimeters long — what is it?
This Italian-American economist taught at MIT's Sloan School and Carnegie Mellon before collecting the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani: Italian-American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2003)
Caused by abnormalities in the genome — a single faulty gene, multiple genes, or a chromosome glitch, inherited or arising de novo — what is the general medical term for this kind of health problem?
Genetic disorder: Health problem from genome abnormalities. It can be caused by a mutation in a single gene (monogenic) or multiple genes (polygenic) or by a chromosome abnormality.

Identified in 1898 by an Italian pathologist and later named in his honor, this cell organelle packages proteins into vesicles and adds sugar chains before shipping them to their destination. What is it called?
Golgi apparatus: Cell organelle that packages proteins for export.
Making its first flight in 2001 and entering Indian Air Force service in 2015, this delta-wing multirole fighter is the smallest and lightest supersonic jet of its generation — which aircraft?
HAL Tejas: Indian combat aircraft. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
This Michigan farm boy left home at 16 for Detroit, later patented the Model T's transmission, and gave his name to a whole system of mass production. Who was he?
This British Egyptologist discovered the untouched tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922 — who is he?
Howard Carter: British archaeologist and Egyptologist (1874–1939)
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
This order of crustaceans includes both seafaring gribbles and the woodlice in your garden, with females brooding their young in a belly pouch called a marsupium. What is it?
Isopoda: Order of arthropods. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

This American physicist worked with Niels Bohr on nuclear fission and had a gift for coinages — "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term that popularized "gravitationally collapsed objects." Who was he?
John Archibald Wheeler: American theoretical physicist (1911–2008)
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
A sweet, aromatic flavouring used in confectionery, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals comes from the root of which legume — though more than a couple of milligrams per kilo a day can cause trouble?
Painlessly swollen lymph nodes, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss point to this family of white-blood-cell cancers, split mainly into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin types — what is it?
Lymphoma: Hematologic cancer that affects lymphocytes.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Typically running 21 to 35 days, this coordinated dance of estrogen and progesterone prepares the uterine lining and releases an egg to make pregnancy possible — what is it?
Menstrual cycle: Natural changes in the human female reproductive system.
Based on a Soviet fighter jet but optimized for ground attack, this variable-sweep aircraft was license-built in India as the 'Bahadur,' or 'Valiant' — which jet?
Mikoyan MiG-27: Series of 1970s Soviet attack aircraft.
Born in China and educated at MIT and Stanford, this billionaire engineer founded Taiwan's dominant chipmaker, serving as its CEO from 1987 to 2005 — who is he?
Morris Chang: Taiwanese businessman and electrical engineer (born 1931)
This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, bringing on excessive daytime sleepiness, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle collapse called cataplexy — what is it?
Narcolepsy: Human sleep disorder. Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.
Unlike its more predictably spreading cousin, this group of blood cancers can appear in multiple parts of the body at once and cause enlarged lymph nodes, fevers, and night sweats — which condition?
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of cancer of lymph nodes.

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
From a single western-Mediterranean flowering plant come both a notorious drug and the tiny dark seeds sprinkled on your bagel — which species is it?
Papaver somniferum: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
Known for its speed, this large crow-sized raptor has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts, and a black head — an avivore with marked sexual dimorphism — what is it?
Peregrine falcon: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey.
Named after the Latin word for the magpie, a bird known for its opportunistic feeding habits, this eating disorder involves craving non-food objects — what is it?
Pica (disorder): Compulsive eating of non-food items.
Nicknamed the 'terror of Bengal' for choking waterways across the world, this South American aquatic plant is commonly known as water hyacinth — what is its scientific name?
Pontederia crassipes: Aquatic plant native to the Amazon basin.

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
Pseudoephedrine: Synthetic decongestant. Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Nicknamed the 'stinking corpse lily,' this Southeast Asian plant genus produces the world's largest flower and was first seen by a Briton in 1818 after a local servant pointed it out — which genus?
This plant genus includes redcurrants, blackcurrants, and gooseberries, and also serves as the main alternate host for a fungal disease that attacks five-needle pines — which genus?
Ribes: Genus of flowering plants in the order Saxifragales.

Also called cot or crib death, this leading cause of infant mortality in the West strikes a baby under one, usually while sleeping between midnight and 9 a.m., and stays unexplained even after a full autopsy. What is it?
SIDS: Sudden unexplained death of a child who is less than one year of age.
A month or so of a diet starved of vitamin C brings on this old deficiency disease — fatigue, sore limbs, and bleeding gums among its hallmarks. What is its scorbutic name?
Scurvy: Disease resulting from a lack of vitamin C.
Named after a Native American war chief, this four-blade, twin-engine Army helicopter entered service in 1979 to replace the Bell UH-1 Iroquois — which aircraft is it?
Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: Series of military utility transport helicopters.

Found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia, this large flightless black bird is a close ratite relative of the emu and ostrich, and its Australian population is listed as endangered — which bird?
Southern cassowary: Species of flightless bird. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.
A cousin of caffeine found in trace amounts in tea, coffee, and chocolate, which methylxanthine drug is used to treat asthma and COPD by blocking adenosine receptors?
Theophylline: Drug used to treat respiratory diseases.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).
Despite a scientific name meaning 'sand burrower,' this snake actually prefers rocky terrain and is considered Europe's most dangerous viper thanks to fangs up to 13mm long — which species?
Vipera ammodytes: Species of snake. It is reputed to be the most dangerous of the European vipers due to its large size, long fangs (up to 13 mm) and high venom toxicity.
In 1879 at the University of Leipzig, this German scholar founded the first formal psychology laboratory, earning him the title 'father of experimental psychology' — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt: German founder of psychology (1832–1920)
Known on the street as flakka or gravel, this synthetic stimulant of the cathinone class was developed in the 1960s and later sold as a designer drug — what is it?
The symbol for iridium is Ir. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.

In what year was A Man Called Otto first released?
